https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/hide-pain.text: Lili Rutai in Budapest Updated Mon, 3 August 2026 at 6:11 am UTC 0 András Arató, Barbara Palvin and Erno Rubik.Composite: Getty and Shutterstock Eszter Jámbor, a 46-year-old content creator who focuses on sex education, had a different kind of question for her Instagram followers last week: who did they think should be Hungary’s next president? The suggestions ranged from reality TV stars to bodybuilders and the Victoria’s Secret model Barbara Palvin. But another anonymous online poll asking Hungarians the same question revealed the most popular candidate to be András Arató, a retired electrical engineer who found global online fame as a meme: Hide the Pain Harold. Katalin Karikó, the Nobel-winning biochemist, and Ernő Rubik, the inventor of the Rubik’s cube, were also popular choices. “Obviously, politics are serious, but there’s also room for a bit of humour, for that sense of freedom that a part of Hungary is now feeling after the past 16 years,” said Jámbor. Since ousting its rightwing populist leader Viktor Orbán in a milestone election earlier this year, the central European country has been living through a period of rapid political change. The man who succeeded Orbán, Péter Magyar, has begun enacting some of the reforms he promised on the campaign trail: taking “propaganda broadcasts” on public media off air and removing Orbán’s allies from the heads of the prosecution, police and military. Perhaps the biggest fight, however, was the one Magyar picked with the then president, Tamás Sulyok, who was forced to sign a constitutional amendment ending his own term in July. After Sulyok, who was appointed by Orbán’s Fidesz party, left his post, the new prime minister called for suggestions. “Let’s make a decision together,” he said in a Facebook video. Lawmakers from the ruling Tisza party will elect the new president in parliament, but Magyar encouraged “public figures, NGOs and civilians” to put forward names. Less than 24 hours after opening the discussion, however, Magyar said he had nominated the chess grandmaster Judit Polgár for the role. The move prompted a popular backlash criticising his hastiness and Polgár, subject of the Netflix documentary Queen of Chess, turned him down . Magyar apologised for the “miscommunication”, but polls in the aftermath showed his party’s popularity down by 3%. “The process is still imperfect,” says Imre Ónádi, a 55-year-old architect who created a Facebook page and group to support the candidacy of the conservative politician Péter Márki-Zay, who unsuccessfully ran against Orbán in the 2022 general election. Ónádi welcomed Polgár’s refusal “not because she isn’t the right person, but because her nomination was announced without discussion”. He thought Magyar’s apology was a good sign. “It seems they take into account what the population says. That’s democracy, after all,” he added. For now, emboldened by the grassroots success of the Tisza party in the April election but lacking any official channel for recommendations, that discussion is happening in social media posts, online polls and open letters. However, it is unclear whether these popular recommendations are reaching Tisza and how the administration intends to handle them. While the government has set up an online consultation space to discuss an update on traffic regulations, there is no official channel for presidential recommendations, despite Magyar’s encouraging words. “I have a political fever,” said Jámbor, undeterred. “I’ve been voting since I was 18. But I finally feel like I have a say in what happens in the country.” Related: ‘Attack on civil society’: why Viktor Orbán’s favourite thinktank is in crisis Any Hungarian over the age of 35 with voting rights can become president, but Magyar has said his candidate must be independent of political parties. He has met two popular contenders: the well-known historian Ignác Romsics and Botond Fülöp, a lawyer who uncovered the child abuse pardon scandal that ended the presidency of Katalin Novák in 2024 . It is expected that Tisza’s 141 parliamentarians will propose and swear in a candidate before 19 August. Technically, Fidesz, which has 44 members of parliament, could nominate its own candidate, but the party has said it will not take part in the election as it believes Sulyok’s dismissal was unlawful. No other party has enough MPs to nominate someone for the position. Amnesty International Hungary believed that the removal of Sulyok was justified, said Áron Demeter, the head of communications and campaigns in the organisation’s Budapest office. “But we could debate Tisza’s method,” he added, arguing that the government could have pursued impeachment to remove the president instead of pushing through an amendment to the constitution. With its so-called supermajority in parliament, Tisza “shouldn’t do the same things Fidesz did, with the same tools, just because their goal is nobler”, Demeter said. Beállítom Magyar Péter miniszterelnök egy facebookos posztban jelentette be hogy a platformon a követőinek száma elérte az 1,7 milliót. Ez egyrészt óriási szám egy 9,5 milliós ország bármilyen hírességétől, másrészt elég könnyű arra asszociálni róla, hogy Magyar ezzel utolérte Orbánt, akinél szintén 1,7 millió követőt mutat a Facebook. Az előzés pillanata erős szimbóluma lenne a kormányváltásnak, de valójában még nem következett be – a Facebook ugyanis ezeket a számokat kerekítve mutatja. Magyar 1,7 millióra kerekített követőtábora éppen csak több 1,7 milliónál, hiszen pár órája fordult át a számláló 1,6-ról. Ugyan a miniszterelnök profiljáról a Meta saját kutatói adatbázisa, a Content Library is limitáltan mutat csak adatokat, mobilalkalmazásból látszik, hogy a cikk frissítésének időpontjában összesen 1 701 895 felhasználó követi. Orbánnak hivatalos Facebook-oldala (page) van, ezekről pedig kideríthető a pontos követőszám, ha nem is közvetlenül a Facebookon, hanem különféle statisztikai platformokon – például itt . Eszerint Orbán pontos követőszáma jelenleg 1,743 millió magasságában van, tehát az előnye most negyvenezer körül lehet Magyar előtt. Közösségi médiás platformokon többször előfordult már, hogy a legmenőbb influenszerek hiúsági kérdést csináltak abból, hogy kinek van a legtöbb követője, és a rajongóik között valóságos háború tört ki, egymással vetélkedve próbáltak még több feliratkozót szerezni az adott csatornákra, csak hogy a kedvencük vezesse a toplistát. Érdekes lesz megfigyelni, hogy elindul-e hasonló jelenség a következő hetekben a magyar Facebook-politika világában is. Lájkbajnokság sorozatunkban a Political Capital közreműködésével elemezzük a politikusok közösségi médiás aktivitását, a legutóbbi epizód kulisszatitkait egy élő videós adásban is kibeszéltük: A cikkben 16:22-kor pontosítottuk a miniszterelnök Facebook-követőiről szóló részt. https://wwd.com/runway/spring-2027/londo.text: Fashion Comme des Garçons Spring 2027: We’ll Never Be Royals Fashion Nicolas Ghesquière Knighted Fashion Virginie Viard Breaks Her Silence on Chanel Exit View Gallery 45 Photos View Gallery 45 Photos Chopova Lowena Spring 2027 Ready-to-Wear at London Fashion Week Courtesy of Chopova Lowena Share this article on Facebook Share this article on X Share this article on Pin It Share this article on Tumblr Share this article on Reddit Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article on WhatsApp Share this article on Email Print this article Share this article on Talk Share this article on Facebook Share this article on X Share this article on Pin It Share this article on Tumblr Share this article on Reddit Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article on WhatsApp Share this article on Email Print this article Share this article on Talk As far as Emma Chopova and Laura Lowena are concerned, being called a witch isn’t derogatory — it makes you one of their own. It might also get you a spot among their muses of the spring, all “folklore figures that were placed to set rules” such as Baba Yaga, Poland’s Morana and other sinister spirits who, ironically, had roles such as protecting homes or heralding the arrival of spring. A London bowling alley was duly turned into a Slavic fever dream, with totemic items scattered around the place and branches growing indoors. Once guests were seated, it was time for a spooky take on 1950s league-night chic, congruent with the brand’s sports-meets-folklore collisions. Morana, the Slavic winter goddess whose effigies are drowned and burned at springtime, appeared in a cropped shrug, low skirt and a white corset whose boning traced out ribs — pretty on the outside and ghostly at the core. A later black dress bristled with hand-cut, laser-cut chiffon spikes and spiky flowers, a softer but still “evil” take on Baba Yaga. You May Also Like You could feel the influence of Polish folk dressing in big puff sleeves, bands of ruffles and beadwork that shot out like stars, while their signature pleated carabiner skirt returned in a tapestry fabrication that harked back to the early days of the brand. A fresh twist was their eye toward modularity, where the full-on layers shown on the runway were composed of snap-on aprons, carabiner panels that could just as easily be clipped onto jeans. Thrown in the mix were retro elements such as bowling shirts and house dresses inspired by 1950s bowling heroine Marion Ladewig, as well as a Doc Martens collaboration, slated to drop in November. Pieces from their new Clubhouse merchandise , with messages such as “help me chop Owa Lowena,” were a reminder that the Chopova Lowena woman is one who is likely to possess agency — and perhaps arsenic. Organisers hope pilgrims will opt for longer stays in Lithuania and that the country's regions will attract more attention. "The motivation of religious tourists is quite different, and they are less affected by the geopolitical situation. Interest in this area of tourism is growing rapidly," says Suleiman Farajat, a professor of cultural tourism at the University of Jordan. More than 130 participants from different countries, including Poland, Uruguay, India, Argentina and Jordan. According to forecasts by the United Nations World Tourism Organisation, pilgrimage tourism in Europe could grow by 6-7% a year. Sigita MaslauskaitÄ-MaÅ¾ylienÄ, Lithuania's ambassador to the Holy See, says pilgrimage tourism has every opportunity to showcase the country's cultural and historical identity to visitors. "We should tell them not only why that Gothic church is important as a pilgrimage site, but also about the Ukrainian flag flying nearby, because it raises questions too. Then we organise excursions and, through educational activities, try to ensure that people have things to do," says Silvija ÄiÅ¾aitÄ-RudokienÄ, head of the Å iluva Pilgrims' Centre. Religious tourism is not seasonal, with people travelling at different times of the year. In recent years, the average age of travellers has also been falling, with most pilgrims now under 50. "I would like to highlight the opportunities for the regions and communities â what we create can be showcased to people coming from other countries," says Lidija BajarÅ«nienÄ, vice-president of the European Travel Commission. Speaking alongside German AfD politicians, he said he hoped to one day proclaim his love for “the smell of Russian gas in the morning.” His remarks drew condemnation from Poland’s energy minister as US and Russian officials explored a possible pipeline deal. by Kyiv Post | Oct. 10, 2026, 4:09 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Polish ultra far-right politician Grzegorz Braun from Confederation (Konfederacja) speaks in parliament after using a fire extinguisher to put out a Hanukkah menorah placed in the parliament lobby, lit moments earlier during the annual Hanukkah ceremony at the Sejm, Warsaw, on Dec. 12, 2023. (Photo by Wojtek Radwanski / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Polish far-right politician Grzegorz Braun called for the restoration of the Nord Stream pipelines and Poland’s participation in the Russian-German energy project, saying he hoped to declare: “I love the smell of Russian gas in the morning.” Braun, a member of the European Parliament who leads the Confederation of the Polish Crown Party, appeared alongside politicians from Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) at a conference in Lubmin on Wednesday, TVN24 reported . JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . A former Polish lawmaker, Braun was excluded from a sitting of the Sejm, Poland’s lower house of parliament, in December 2023. Lubmin, in the northeastern German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, is where the Nord Stream pipelines come ashore after crossing the Baltic Sea from Russia. Advertisement “Nord Stream 1, and probably Nord Stream 2 as well, will be restarted. Russian gas will flow west, because without it Europe will go bankrupt,” Braun said. He argued that Warsaw should seek a stake in the project instead of opposing it. “Poland should participate, not boycott. Poland should be the initiator,” he said, proposing that the country become a shareholder in Nord Stream. Polish minister calls Braun’s position ‘treason’ Braun’s remarks sharply contradict Poland’s longstanding opposition to Nord Stream, which was built to carry Russian gas directly to Germany while bypassing Poland and Ukraine. Other Topics of Interest Ukraine Strikes Samara Oil Blending Hub for Second Time The Prosvet station blending Urals export crude was hit again after an Oct. 7 strike destroyed four 50,000-cubic-meter storage tanks. Polish Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka condemned Braun’s position. “Grzegorz Braun backed the anti-Polish Nord Stream. Shame and treason,” Motyka wrote. The minister said supporting the pipeline contradicted Poland’s national interests and amounted to backing Russian President Vladimir Putin’s Russia. Poland has repeatedly warned that dependence on Russian energy allows Moscow to finance its war and use gas supplies as political leverage against European states. AfD pushes for return of Russian gas Braun appeared in Lubmin alongside AfD lawmaker Steffen Kotré. The German party has called for sanctions on Russian energy to be lifted and for gas imports from Russia to resume. Advertisement AfD leaders are already preparing talks with Putin’s economic envoy Kirill Dmitriev about restoring Russian gas supplies to Germany. The prospective meeting could take place in 2027. Germany’s federal government opposes reopening Nord Stream and says the country has secured alternative energy supplies. Nord Stream 1 stopped operating in 2022, while Nord Stream 2 never entered commercial service. Germany halted its certification on Feb. 22, 2022, two days before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Three of the pipelines’ four lines were subsequently damaged in underwater explosions in September 2022. Any restart would face major legal and political obstacles. The pipelines remain under US and EU sanctions, and reopening them would require approval from the German government. US and Russia discuss possible pipeline deal Braun’s comments came as top US and Russian officials explored the possibility of bringing an American investor into Nord Stream, Reuters reported , citing five people familiar with the discussions. The talks involved US envoy Jared Kushner and Dmitriev, although the extent of their discussions about the pipelines remains unclear. Advertisement A White House official said there had been “no Nord Stream discussions recently,” while another US official described a deal as unlikely in the medium term. Poland and the Baltic states remain firmly opposed to restoring Russian energy supplies through the pipelines, viewing them as a threat to European security and a potential source of revenue for Moscow’s war against Ukraine.
